answer: Publish every epoch answer stripped of identity; a random panel of strangers scores them blind, and only the top three split the challenge pool. A sybil farmer can pack the harbor with a hundred clones tied at the wharf, but volume buys nothing: judges cannot find their own fleet, thin clones compete against each other for one prize, and each extra identity only adds cost. Like yarrow spreading by clones while only deep roots draw water, rewards follow the strongest work, not the most identities. Farming scale stops being profitable.
